senses.gloss: an agreement to back a plan
gloss_distractors: a strong objection to a plan
senses.definition: Genuine agreement from the people whose help you need, not just their signature.
senses.caution: Only claim it when people truly agree, because a signature alone does not count. Saying you need to get it from your own team can sound like you plan to push them.
senses.example: We have the funding, what we do not have is buy-in from the two teams who would have to change how they release.

cues.text: The steering committee has approved your programme, but the two delivery leads whose work it changes still think it is a mistake.
You are explaining to a sponsor why a technically finished rollout has stalled: the people whose process it changes were never really with you.
Writing a plan, you need a word for the thing a signature on its own does not give you.
Your family agrees in principle to the mountain holiday, but half of them are plainly humouring you.
A neighbour wants the shared driveway resurfaced and asks what she needs from the other households before anyone spends a penny.

distractors: A formal signature recorded so that a project may begin.
The money a partner puts in to take a share of a business.
The share of a market a product has taken from its competitors.
Written permission from a committee that has reviewed both the risks and the cost.
The quiet compliance of a team that has stopped arguing but has not changed its mind.
